name: Score cold-chain batch recall risk from IoT excursions with Anthropic and email

parameters.content:
## Cold-Chain Predictive Recall

This workflow predicts WHICH shipped batches are likely compromised by cold-chain temperature excursions, using live IoT sensor data plus route/shipment history - before lab testing confirms spoilage.

### Who's it for
- Cold-chain logistics teams (pharma, vaccines, food, biologics) who need to act on a shipment BEFORE it reaches the shelf, not after a customer complaint
- Quality assurance teams who want a real-sensor-based predictive triage layer on top of, not instead of, lab testing
- Ops teams who want to route only the batches that actually need attention to the QA queue instead of manually reviewing every temperature log

### How it works
1. A schedule trigger polls for active in-transit shipments on an interval
2. Two APIs are called in parallel: the shipment/route data for each active batch (from a TMS/ERP-style system), and the live IoT sensor readings (temperature/humidity) for that batch's tracker
3. JS - Build Cold-Chain Excursion Profile turns raw sensor readings into a clean profile: total excursion time outside the validated range, max deviation, Mean Kinetic Temperature (the standard cold-chain QA metric), and a route risk factor from transfer hubs and transit duration
4. JS - Run Spoilage Risk Monte Carlo runs 1,000 randomized simulations of product degradation using Q10 reaction-kinetics, sampling sensor noise and product-sensitivity uncertainty each run, to produce a distribution of likely ending potency and a probability the batch falls below its spoilage threshold
5. AI turns the raw simulation output into a plain-English risk classification (Safe / Monitor / Quarantine / Recall) and concrete next steps
6. High-risk batches (Quarantine/Recall) trigger an immediate urgent alert email in addition to the full predictive recall report - so QA can hold a batch before it ever reaches lab confirmation

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n
2. Add Anthropic Claude credentials and attach to the Anthropic model node
3. Add your TMS/ERP API credentials to Fetch Active Shipments & Route History and replace the placeholder URL/auth
4. Add your IoT platform API key to Fetch Live IoT Sensor Readings and replace YOUR_IOT_PLATFORM_API_KEY
5. Add SMTP credentials to both email nodes and replace the from/to addresses with your QA and ops distribution lists
6. Adjust the schedule trigger interval to match how often your IoT platform reports new readings
7. Activate the workflow

### Requirements
- Anthropic Claude API key (claude-sonnet-4 recommended)
- A TMS/ERP or shipment-tracking API that exposes active shipments, route history, and each product's validated temperature range
- An IoT/cold-chain sensor platform API that exposes per-batch temperature (and ideally humidity) readings
- SMTP credentials for report and alert delivery

## Stage 1: Live Sensor Data & Excursion Profile

Schedule - Poll Active Shipments fires on an interval to check every batch currently in transit.

Fetch Active Shipments & Route History (API 1) and Fetch Live IoT Sensor Readings (API 2) run in parallel off the schedule trigger.

Merge - Combine Shipment & Sensor Data joins both API responses into a single item per batch.

JS - Build Cold-Chain Excursion Profile (Code Node 1) computes total time outside the validated temperature range, max deviation, Mean Kinetic Temperature, and a route risk factor from transfer hubs and transit duration.

## Stage 2: Predictive Spoilage Risk Engine

JS - Run Spoilage Risk Monte Carlo (Code Node 2) runs 1,000 randomized simulations of Q10 reaction-kinetics degradation, sampling sensor measurement noise and product-sensitivity uncertainty on each run.

Each path tracks projected ending potency, then the results are summarized as P10/P50/P90 ending potency and a probability the batch falls below its spoilage threshold.

Wait - Simulation Buffer (Wait Node 1) pauses briefly before the AI call to respect API rate limits.

## Stage 3: AI Classification & Alerting

The classification AI (claude-sonnet-4, temperature 0.3) turns the excursion profile and simulation output into a plain-English narrative, a risk level (Safe/Monitor/Quarantine/Recall), and recommended actions.

JS - Parse AI Output & Format Predictive Recall Report (Code Node 3) extracts the structured JSON safely, with a rule-based fallback keyed off the spoilage probability if AI parsing fails.

IF - High Risk Batch? checks whether the batch was classified Quarantine or Recall. High-risk batches get an immediate Send Urgent Recall Alert Email in addition to the standard Send Batch Risk Report Email that every batch receives.

parameters.text:
=You are a cold-chain quality assurance assistant reviewing a predictive spoilage risk simulation for a shipped batch, based on live IoT sensor data and route history - before lab testing confirms anything.

Batch: {{ $json.batchId }} ({{ $json.productType }})
Shipment ID: {{ $json.shipmentId }}
Validated Temperature Range: {{ $json.tempRangeMin }}C to {{ $json.tempRangeMax }}C

Cold-Chain Profile:
Total Excursion Time: {{ $json.excursionMinutes }} minutes
Max Deviation From Range: {{ $json.maxDeviationC }}C
Mean Kinetic Temperature: {{ $json.meanKineticTempC }}C
Transfer Hubs: {{ $json.transferHubsCount }} | Shipment Duration: {{ $json.shipmentDurationHours }} hours
Route Risk Factor: {{ $json.routeRiskFactor }}

Simulated Outcomes ({{ $json.simulation.iterations }} Monte Carlo runs):
P10 (pessimistic) ending potency: {{ $json.simulation.p10EndingPotencyPct }}%
P50 (median) ending potency: {{ $json.simulation.p50EndingPotencyPct }}%
P90 (optimistic) ending potency: {{ $json.simulation.p90EndingPotencyPct }}%
Probability batch falls below the {{ $json.simulation.spoilageThresholdPctPotency }}% potency threshold: {{ $json.simulation.spoilageProbabilityPct }}%

Classify this batch and explain your reasoning in plain English for a warehouse operations team that is not scientific.

Return a JSON object with EXACTLY these fields:
{
  "riskLevel": "One of: Safe, Monitor, Quarantine, Recall",
  "narrativeSummary": "3-4 sentences, plain English, specific to these numbers",
  "recommendedActions": ["short actionable recommendation 1", "short actionable recommendation 2", "short actionable recommendation 3"]
}

Return ONLY the JSON. No markdown, no explanation.
